source.sectionTitle: Neisseria meningitidis is transmitted by PROLONGED (generally >8 hours)

record.item: Neisseria meningitidis is transmitted by PROLONGED (generally >8 hours)
record.source_text:
Neisseria meningitidis is transmitted by PROLONGED (generally >8 hours) 
DIRECT CLOSE CONTACT (<1 metre) 
with LARGE-DROPLET RESPIRATORY SECRETIONS of an infected individual. 
The INFECTION CONTROL DEPARTMENT must be informed immediately. 
Notification can be based on either CLINICAL SUSPICION of meningococcal infection 
OR LABORATORY CONFIRMATION. 
Infection Control Protocol | Neisseria 
Meningitidis 
 
The primary means for prevention of sporadic cases of meningococcal disease is SELECTIVE 
ANTIMICROBIAL CHEMOPROPHYLAXIS LIMITED TO SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES ONLY. 
Antimicrobial chemoprophylaxis should ONLY be offered to CLOSE CONTACTS of infected patients DEFINED AS: 
1. Anyone DIRECTLY EXPOSED TO THE PATIENT’S ORAL SECRETIONS, even if contact is 
transient. 
a) Kissing 
b) Sharing of food or beverages or eating utensils 
c) Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation 
d) Endotracheal intubation; and/or 
e) Endotracheal tube management 
 
2. HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS 
(persons sleeping in the same dwelling, sharing eating utensils) 
3. INSTITUTIONAL CONTACTS sharing sleeping quarters or kitchen 
(boarding schools, military camps, barracks) 
4. NURSERY SCHOOL or DAY CARE CENTRE CLOSE CONTACTS ONLY 
(both pupils & teachers who share a classroom) 
 
 
The aim of chemoprophylaxis is to prevent secondary cases by eliminating the nasopharyngeal carriage 
of the organism. 
• 
Because the rate of secondary disease for close contacts is highest during the first few days after 
onset of disease in the index patient, chemoprophylaxis should be administered as soon as 
possible (ideally within 24 hours after identification of the index patient) 
• 
Chemoprophylaxis administered >14 days after onset of illness in the index patient is ineffective. 
 
Neisseria meningitidis is a NOTIFIABLE DISEASE. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
References 
1. 
Adapted from CDC/ WHO GUIDELINES 
 
 
 
This includes: 
• 
Isolation in a separate cubicle 
• 
Wearing of surgical masks when entering cubicle 
• 
Use of eye protection to protect against exposure to secretions/droplets 
• 
Gloves should be worn for all contact 
• 
Hand washing must occur before and after patient contact 
THE PATIENT MAY BE DE-ISOLATED AFTER 24 HOURS THERAPY WITH 
AGENTS THAT RELIABLY ERADICATE 
NASOPHARYNGEAL CARRIAGE (Ceftriaxone/Cefotaxime). 
Patients treated with Penicillin G alone cannot be de-isolated UNTIL they receive 
chemoprophylaxis with an appropriate antibiotic to eradicate nasopharyngeal carriage (refer to 
antibiotics table). 
Procedure to be followed BEFORE instituting CHEMOPROPHYLAXIS 
1. NOTIFY THE INFECTION CONTROL DEPARTMENT of the TYPE OF EXPOSURE 
i.e. respiratory droplet, mucosal splash, percutaneous. 
2. The infection control department will advise on the necessity of antimicrobial chemoprophylaxis. 
This will limit the practice of unnecessary and indiscriminate use of antibiotics. 
NB Mass chemoprophylaxis for those who have not been in close 
contact with index patient is unwarranted and not recommended! 
3. Staff
